questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
Digital Light synthesis (DLS) is a form of additive manufacturing that utilizes light to rapidly cure liquid resin into high-quality, 3D objects. Step 1: Ultraviolet (UV) light images are projected up into a pool of liquid resin, where the object's first layer takes shape. Step 2: The partially cured resin object is raised, creating a thin space (a "dead zone") beneath it for oxygen and liquid resin to flow through. Step 3: The UV light passes through the dead zone—maintaining the flow of resin—and partially cures additional layers of the object. Step 4: When the resin object is complete, it is baked in an oven to complete the curing.
questions.prompt: The student wants to describe how DLS cures 3D objects. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: DLS cures 3D objects by passing through a "dead zone," adding layers to the object, then curing the object in an oven.
choices.B: In DLS, UV light is projected into layers of liquid resin until the resin solidifies and passes through a "dead zone," wherein the curing is completed.
choices.C: In DLS, UV light images are projected into a liquid resin pool to cure a 3D object layer by layer; once solidified, the object is baked in an oven.
choices.D: DLS is a form of additive manufacturing that rapidly cures liquid resin into a 3D object in which UV light solidifies layer by layer before being baked in an oven, creating a high-quality, 3D object.
